keyChanges.title: Elluswamy posts '10 million robots' correction as Giga Texas factory rises — no production numbers disclosed
keyChanges.description: On July 31, 2026, Tesla Optimus chief Ashok Elluswamy posted a terse 'Correction, 10 million robots' on X, clarifying the long-term annual capacity target for the dedicated Optimus factory under construction at Giga Texas (not the Fremont pilot line, which targets 1M/yr). The post was covered by Teslarati and Basenor. Separately, Basenor published a Giga Texas construction update covering drone footage through July 27, 2026: a multi-story steel superstructure is rising across the 5.2M sq-ft site, seven large cranes operating simultaneously, and floor decking installation is underway — construction pace described as accelerated, not standard commercial build. The Fremont footprint had grown to ~360 ft north-to-south by July 13. Context that makes these headlines misleading: (1) Elluswamy's '10M robots' post adds zero new information — Musk cited this figure repeatedly since at least mid-2025; it is a long-term aspirational target for a factory that does not produce a single unit yet; (2) The Giga Texas construction milestone (Volume production target: Summer 2027) is a facility update, not a production start; (3) No Optimus unit count, production rate, takt time, yield, or Academy delivery total has been disclosed by Tesla since the Q2 earnings call on July 22; (4) The Fremont line status as of week ending Aug 6 remains: 'installing first-generation lines' per Q2 letter language — no official correction to 'production started.' The late-July/August window Musk set on Q1 earnings as the production start target has now elapsed or is elapsing with no official confirmation of first robot output.

positive_signals: Giga Texas Optimus factory construction visibly accelerating: 7 simultaneous cranes, floor decking in, multi-story steel structure through July 27
Elluswamy's correction reconfirms 10M/yr long-term Texas capacity target, signaling program is intact
Two-site manufacturing strategy (Fremont 1M + Texas 10M) structurally on track from a facilities standpoint
negative_signals: No Optimus unit count, production rate, or takt time disclosed in period — production count remains effectively zero from an external verifiable standpoint
Fremont late-July/August production start window per Q1 earnings has elapsed with no official 'production started' announcement from Tesla
Elluswamy's '10M robots' post is a restatement of a previously known aspirational target, not a new milestone
Giga Texas produces zero robots; earliest volume production still Summer 2027
V3 (Gen 3) Optimus still unrevealed publicly — no design finalization confirmation for volume production
Q2 letter language ('installing first-generation lines,' 'production soon/later this year') has not been upgraded to a start confirmation
No Optimus Academy unit count, task performance data, or training data collection metrics released

key_metrics.actual: 0 confirmed units produced from Fremont first-gen line; Giga Texas in construction (7 cranes, floor decking installed as of July 27)
key_metrics.target: Fremont: production start late July–August 2026 (Q1 guidance, now elapsed); Giga Texas: volume production Summer 2027; long-term: 1M/yr Fremont + 10M/yr Texas
key_metrics.trajectory: Construction infrastructure progressing on schedule but production line commissioning at Fremont unconfirmed; ramp still 'flat and long' per Musk

keyChanges.title: BYD debuts Xiao Di humanoid robot in August — direct Optimus competitor now commercially deployed while Tesla still pre-production
keyChanges.description: BYD confirmed and deployed its first humanoid robot, Xiao Di, at its 'Di Space' showroom in Zhengzhou in early August 2026. Multiple sources corroborate the announcement and deployment: TechNode (July 27), kr-asia, The Next Web, Notebookcheck, and Stuff South Africa (August 5 teaser update). Key details: Xiao Di stands 1.61m tall, weighs 58.5kg, has 31 degrees of freedom, and features real-time multilingual translation (6 Chinese dialects + 6 foreign languages), 360-degree vision, and an onboard AI model for object/facial recognition. BYD's plan is to deploy 2-3 units per BYD dealership, with the robot greeting customers and explaining vehicles. BYD made clear this is a fully functional prototype, not a concept. US government is reportedly blocking BYD's access to the US market before the debut. The competitive significance for Optimus: BYD — a company with supply chain scale, actuator sourcing, and manufacturing depth that Tesla explicitly lacks for Optimus — is now commercially deploying a humanoid robot while Tesla cannot confirm a single Fremont Optimus unit has come off the line. Chinese competitors (Unitree G1 at $17,990 on Amazon; BYD Xiao Di for dealerships) are advancing commercial use cases while Tesla is still in 'installing lines' and 'Optimus Academy training data collection' phases. This directly validates the competitive risk flagged in last week's earnings context and worsens the timeline gap between Tesla's promises and commercial reality.

positive_signals: BYD's entry validates the humanoid robot market opportunity Tesla is targeting
Xiao Di is a limited-use dealership greeter, not a general-purpose factory robot — different use case than Optimus's industrial/household target
US market access reportedly blocked for BYD robot, reducing direct near-term competition on Tesla's home turf
negative_signals: BYD — still behind Tesla in AI but far ahead in supply chain depth and actuator sourcing — is now commercially deploying a humanoid robot while Tesla cannot confirm Fremont production has started
Xiao Di is already working in BYD showrooms; Optimus first builds are still destined for internal Optimus Academy training data collection
Chinese manufacturers (BYD, Unitree, Xpeng Iron, Chery Aimoga) are collectively advancing the sector with commercial revenue while Tesla remains pre-revenue on Optimus
Unitree G1 listed at $17,990 on Amazon — if Chinese price competition scales, Tesla's $20,000-$25,000 cost floor at 1M/yr is already at parity or worse with a shipping product
Supply chain decoupling risk: Tesla's Optimus BOM could rise from ~$46k to ~$131k if forced off Chinese component suppliers (actuators, reducers, batteries)
BYD's deployment pace (2-3 units per dealership chain-wide) implies meaningful scale faster than Tesla's Academy-first approach

categoryUpdate.latestStatus: Fremont first-gen Optimus production lines still being installed as of late July 2026; no official production start confirmed despite late-July/August target window from Q1 earnings having elapsed. Giga Texas dedicated factory construction accelerating (7 cranes, multi-story steel, floor decking through July 27). No unit counts, yield, takt time, or Academy delivery numbers disclosed. V3/Gen 3 still unrevealed. BYD Xiao Di commercially deployed in August while Tesla remains pre-revenue.
categoryUpdate.nextMilestone: Official confirmation of first Fremont line robot output and Optimus Academy unit delivery; V3 public reveal (no date set); Giga Texas volume production (Summer 2027 target)
concerns: Late-July/August production start window from Q1 earnings has elapsed with no official start confirmation — silent slip pattern identical to Q2 letter dropping 'volume production in 2026' language
Zero unit counts or production rate disclosures; no third-party verification of any Fremont first-gen output
BYD and Chinese competitors (Unitree, Xpeng) are commercially deploying humanoid robots while Tesla remains in training-data-collection phase
Supply chain remains Tesla's self-described 'hardest challenge' — no updates on progress insourcing critical actuator/reducer components since Q2 call
Chinese supply chain decoupling risk: BOM could increase 2-3x if US-China trade restrictions tighten further
V3 still unrevealed — no confirmation that volume production design is finalized
